subject: Ledger timestamp skew & entity attribution — GCP marketplace invoice
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@acme-analytics.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Discrepancy on Sept GCP marketplace invoice — entity attribution

Hi Alex,

We just closed our September close and are seeing a ~$28k variance between the GCP marketplace invoice and the settlement statement Redwood sent. A few lines on the invoice look like they were attributed to the wrong internal project (project rename earlier this quarter), so the invoice shows usage under Acme-legacy-project-123 while our ledger has it under acme-data-prod.

I've attached our usage export (acme-usage-export-2028-09.csv) + the PDF of the GCP Marketplace invoice (gcp-marketplace-invoice-2028-09.pdf). Key facts:
- Invoice ID: GCP-INV-2028-09-3321
- Total invoice: $187,412.13
- Lines affected (approx): $28,127.40 across 4 metered lines

Can you help triage? When we try to match by usage_id we either get no match or multiple hits in Redwood's payout ledger. We need a clear mapping to finalize our payout reconciliation.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20 min call if helpful.

Sara Liu
Finance Manager, Acme Analytics

Attachments: acme-usage-export-2028-09.csv (CSV, 42KB), gcp-marketplace-invoice-2028-09.pdf (PDF, 210KB)

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Sept GCP marketplace invoice — entity attribution

Hi Sara — thanks for the detailed packet.

Quick acknowledgement: we're looking into this. Marissa and Jonas will run match-and-diff against our settlement ledger and the Marketplace invoice lines. Laura, can you confirm whether Treasury/Collections saw any related payout hold for Acme in September?

Preliminary asks to make triage faster:
- If you can highlight 2–3 invoice lines (invoice_line_id) that you want prioritized, that will speed our root-cause.
- Can you confirm whether the project rename happened before or after 2028-09-15? Project rename timing affects how GCP maps project labels to usage rows.

Next steps: Jonas will share an exported ledger slice and we will loop in GCP billing if we see duplicates or ingestion retries. If it helps, I can open the marketplace support case from our side to get logs of metering ID mapping.

I'll follow up within EOD PT with an initial reconciliation table.

Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0123

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Oct 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Sept GCP marketplace invoice — entity attribution

Hi Sara / Alex / team —

Thanks for sending the files. I pulled the relevant ledger slice for Acme and did an initial match against the usage_id column in your CSV. Summary of what I found:

- We can match ~92% of the invoice lines exactly by usage_id + timestamp.
- There are 4 invoice lines (line ids: L-9823, L-9824, L-9825, L-9826) totalling $28,127.40 where GCP shows project=Acme-legacy-project-123 but our ledger routes to acme-data-prod. The root cause appears to be a partially-duplicated metering ingestion on 2028-09-17 03:14:xx UTC (one ingestion record retained the old project name, another record had the new project label).

Attached is a CSV export (redwood-ledger-acme-2028-09-skew.csv) that contains: ledger_line_id, usage_id, invoice_line_id, billed_amount_cents, recorded_project_label, ingestion_uuid. The ingestion_uuid for the duplicated lines is distinct but maps to the same usage_id in two different rows — this is why your matching by usage_id produced multiple hits.

Proposed fix options:
- Fast path (preferred by customers): we coordinate with GCP Marketplace Billing Ops to request a marketplace reclassification on their side so the invoice lines consolidate under the canonical project label (Acme Data Prod). This keeps the invoice unchanged but allows settlements to align.
- Ledger correction: we can apply an internal ledger reclassification (audit note + journal entry) to map legacy project labels to the canonical entity for the affected invoice. This requires sign-off from Finance and is visible on the next payout cycle.

Karthik — can you advise on the expected timelines for internal journaling/sign-off? Laura — FYI for payout timeline impact; if we postpone sign-off, Acme may have a short-term balance variance on their next remittance.

Next steps:
1) Sara — please confirm you want us to open the marketplace case with GCP (we can include your attach packet and request reclassification).
2) If you prefer ledger correction, reply with a confirmation email that GCP will not require a formal refund/credit (we'll prepare a JV).

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-ledger-acme-2028-09-skew.csv (CSV, 28KB)

From: GCP Marketplace Billing Ops <billing@google.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@acme-analytics.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Oct 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on Sept GCP marketplace invoice — entity attribution

Hi Sara / Alex / Jonas —

Thanks for the packet and the ledger export. We reviewed the invoice (GCP-INV-2028-09-3321) and the ingestion logs for 2028-09-17. Our telemetry shows a transient metering ingestion retry caused by a project label change during an automated rename operation. The retry created two separate ingestion records for the same usage_id; one record retained the old label (Acme-legacy-project-123), the other recorded acme-data-prod.

Impact and remediation options we can perform from the marketplace side:
- Option A (preferred): Perform a reclassification request that consolidates the two ingestion records to the canonical project label on the invoice. This will generate an updated invoice PDF and a marketplace reclassification confirmation note. Expected SLA: 7–10 business days after we receive an authorized request from the seller (Acme).
- Option B: Issue a credit/memo for the affected invoice lines if seller prefers not to reissue the invoice. This requires a signed request and may require additional verification (copy of ledger export + authorized signer). Expected SLA: 10–15 business days.

Support case: MP-SUPPORT-1142789
Required artifacts to proceed (please attach to the case):
- Seller authorization (email from Acme finance or DocuSign)
- Seller ledger slice showing canonical project mapping (Jonas' csv is fine)

If you want us to proceed with Option A, reply with: 
"Acme authorizes marketplace reclassification to project label: acme-data-prod" and we will start the process.

Let us know and we will attach the reclassification request to MP-SUPPORT-1142789.

Best,
GCP Marketplace Billing Ops
Billing Support Engineer — Marketplace QA
billing@google.com
